text: %@ and %@ can't open at the same time. Add a pause between them in Order, Pauses & If.
%@ and %@ change the same switch, so only the last one sticks.
%lu assignments, %lu menus, %lu shell commands, %lu URLs or Shortcuts.
A banner names what just ran. Haptic Feedback is a small tap; it follows iOS's System Haptics setting.
A button press, a swipe, or something that happens, like plugging in your charger.
A menu pops up a list of actions to choose from. Assign it to a trigger from the action picker's Menus category. Swipe left on a menu to delete it.
A menu pops up a list of actions to choose from. Make one, then assign it to a trigger from the action picker.
Actions run top to bottom. Drag to reorder. Tap an action to add a pause after it or to run it only if something is true; tap an If to change it or add Otherwise.
All of these must be true, or it does its normal thing.
Any URL or URL scheme, e.g. https://…, tel:… or music://
Anywhere runs %@; picking here replaces it %@.
Apps and Shortcuts always wait for you to unlock. With this on, shell commands wait too.
Assigned presses replace the button's own action.
Assigned presses run alongside the button's own action.
Battery level, 1–100 %. Runs once when the level climbs past it; 100 means fully charged.
Battery level, 1–100 %. Runs once when the level falls past it.
Clears every assignment, menu and setting, and turns off Allow API (Replace Button Actions goes back on). Saved profiles are kept.
Device name, as shown in Settings → Bluetooth
Double and Triple Press take over Wallet and the Accessibility Shortcut.
Every assignment, menu and setting is cleared. Saved profiles are kept.
Experimental on Face ID iPhones, so it starts off: a tap at the top can begin pulling down Control Center. Double Tap and Hold always work.
Export makes a file you can send with AirDrop, Messages or Files. Import replaces your current setup after showing what it contains.
For one place only (Home Screen, apps, Lock Screen), open that place above instead.
Give one app its own assignments: inside it they replace In Apps' and Anywhere's for the same trigger, everywhere else nothing changes.
It includes the Wi-Fi network and Bluetooth device names used in your events.
It includes your shell commands; check they don't contain anything private.
Lets other tweaks and the triggr command run your triggers and built-in actions (never commands or apps). Leave off unless you use it.
Lets the status bar's single-tap triggers run. Double Tap and Hold always work.
Lower brightness by this much each time, 1–50 % (10 is a good step)
Most things belong in Anywhere. Use a place when a trigger should do something different there.
Name shown at the top of the menu
Network name (SSID), as shown in Settings → Wi-Fi
No actions yet: pick some first.
No custom events yet. Add one below, then pick what it runs.
No speakers or TVs found right now. You can still type a name.
Nothing picked: it does its normal thing (%@).
Nothing picked: it does its normal thing (%@). An action you pick runs instead. To keep %@ some of the time, add Only If.
Nothing runs after a restart or power off. Keep it last.
Nothing set up yet. Add a Trigger to start, or open the Guide to see what Triggr can do.
On: Shortcuts run like Back Tap runs them, without opening the app. Off: the Shortcuts app opens.
On: an assigned press runs instead of the button's own action. Off: both run. Waking, Emergency SOS and force restart always work.
Only %@. Replaces %@ for the same trigger.
Optional. For example: only while the flashlight is on, only on your home Wi-Fi, or only at night.
Pauses go between two actions. Pick at least two actions first, or tap an action to add a pause after it.
Pick a button or gesture, then what it does. It works everywhere, unless you give it something else in one of the Places.
Raise brightness by this much each time, 1–50 % (10 is a good step)
Remove all %lu assignments %@? Those triggers go back to their normal behaviour.
Respring and Safe Mode restart SpringBoard, so actions after them won't run. Keep them last.
Respring, Restart and Power Off ask before they run, from a trigger or from Run Now. Safe Mode never asks, so it always works when a tweak gets stuck.
Runs at this time on the selected days. iOS can delay timers while the phone sleeps; if it's more than 5 minutes late, it's skipped.
Runs instead of the plain icon flick in that direction.
Safe Mode restarts SpringBoard with no tweaks, Triggr included, until you tap Dismiss on the Safe Mode screen.
Save and switch setups, share them as a file, or reset Triggr to its defaults.
Saves your current assignments, menus and settings. An existing profile with this name is replaced.
Seconds to wait before the next action (0.1–%g).
Shell command. Runs with the jailbreak's sh -c as the mobile user.
Shortcut name, exactly as in the Shortcuts app
Shown in a small banner. {battery}, {time} and {date} are filled in.
Single taps are off in Options.
Speaker or TV name, as it appears in the AirPlay menu (part of it is enough)
SpringBoard crashed while Triggr was handling the Action button, so the button went back to iOS. It tries again after the next Triggr update. Your other triggers still work.
Start and end, 24-hour, e.g. 22:00-06:00 (overnight is fine)
Swipe left on an event to delete it.
Swipe right on a trigger, or hold it, to run it without pressing anything.
Tap a profile to switch to it or export it; swipe left to delete it. Switching saves your current setup into the active profile first, so nothing is lost.
Tap an action below. Pick several to run them in order.
Tap one to change it, or swipe left to remove it.
Tap one to change it. Swipe right or hold it to run it now, swipe left to remove it.
Tap the actions this menu should offer.
Text for the device to say
Text to show in an alert
That file isn't a setup exported from Triggr.
This replaces your current setup. Save it as a profile first if you want to keep it.
This restarts or powers off the phone as soon as the trigger fires, without asking. The jailbreak stays off until you run Dopamine again.
This setup runs shell commands on your device. Only import setups from people you trust.
To run instead, turn on Replace Button Actions in Options.
Triggr ignores triggers while one of these apps is open, like a game that uses the volume buttons.
Triggr reacts only to the triggers you add. Everything else works as usual.
Turn on the flashlight, open an app or run a shortcut. Pick a few and they run in order.
Wait this many seconds, then run only if the opposite didn't happen meanwhile (e.g. you didn't rejoin the network).
